To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) social behavior is often triggered automatically by social stimuli, and (2) social behavior is triggered automatically by social perceptions.

(1) the mere perception of a social stimulus (e.g., an elderly person) can activate social knowledge (e.g., about elderly people) and that this activation in turn can affect social behavior (e.g., walking more slowly).

(1) the perception of social stimuli automatically activates the corresponding social behaviors, (2) these automatic effects are not mediated by conscious awareness, and (3) the effects are mediated by the automatic spreading activation process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how social behavior is regulated.
how social perception and social cognition influence social behavior, in particular, with how the perception and cognition of social stimuli automatically influence social behavior.
the automaticity of social perception and social behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the perception-behavior link exists, but is not automatic and is not a direct link.
there is no conclusive evidence that social cognition has any effects on behavior.
social perception and behavior are inextricably connected and that social behavior can be influenced automatically by social perception.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are interested in the automaticity of social behavior.
social perception and social behavior are more closely linked than previously thought.
the automaticity of social perception is a two-way street, with social perception automatically affecting social behavior, but also with social behavior automatically affecting social perception.
The main takeaway from our work is that
people’s behavior is influenced by the social information that is automatically perceived in the environment.
social perception and social behavior are not separate processes but rather two aspects of one process.
the automaticity of social perception is not limited to the automatic activation of social concepts and stereotypes.
